title: assert()
summary: Guards an assumption: errors with your message if the value is falsy, otherwise returns the value unchanged. Inline nil-guard and invariant check in one.

details.heading: Falsiness rule
details.body: Only `nil` and `false` fail the assertion — `0` and `""` pass. Custom messages make failures self-explanatory in Output.

explanation.whatItIs: 'I expect this to be true; if not, stop everything and tell me exactly what assumption broke.'
explanation.whyItExists: Loud, early failure at the point of the assumption beats mysterious nil errors twenty lines later.
whenToUse: Validating function inputs that must be present
whenNotToUse: For expected-absent cases (FindFirstChild misses are normal — handle nil instead)
In hot paths where the check is redundant
As flow control — assert is for 'impossible' states
tips: Always write a message: `assert(x, "x must exist before round start")`
assert returns its value, so it composes: `local h = assert(char:FindFirstChild("Humanoid"))`
commonMistakes: Using assert where a soft fallback is needed — assert raises, it doesn't branch
Forgetting the message and getting 'assertion failed!' with no clue

examples.title: Inline guards
examples.code:
local function beginRound()
    local map = assert(workspace:FindFirstChild("Map"), "Map missing!")
    local spawn = assert(map:FindFirstChild("Spawn"), "Spawn point missing in Map!")
    print("Round begins at", spawn.Position)
end
examples.whyItWorks: If either lookup fails, the script halts right there with a message naming the missing piece — no downstream nil mystery.
